name: atom-jepa-bio
protocol: 5 x 5 GroupKFold over chemical clusters, one fixed holdout, Tukey HSD

reports.title: Bioassays Before ADMET
reports.question: Does a second pre-training stage on 1,089 PCBA bioassays make the Atom-JEPA encoder better at ADMET, and does it overtake Monroe + TabPFN 3?
reports.takeaway: Yes, mostly. The authors' count reproduces within one, 35 of 45 best or tied against Monroe's 17. Swapping the checkpoint helps fine-tuning on 32 of 45 paired calls and hurts on one, most on Biogen, where a 3-ahead, 13-behind deficit against Monroe becomes 12 ahead, 3 behind. Caco-2 and MLM stay Monroe's.
reports.summary: Atom-JEPA-Bio continues the released Atom-JEPA encoder with the same self-supervised objectives plus a focal loss over 1,089 PCBA bioassays, and fine-tunes it with the unchanged recipe. Run here with the authors' code and weights, it is compared with stage-1 Atom-JEPA, fine-tuned and frozen, with Monroe + TabPFN 3, and with the authors' own scoreboard, with a machine re-run check and a split of the Biogen test set by PCBA membership.
reports.finding: Over the authors' six arms, fine-tuned Bio is best or tied on 35 of 45 combinations (their figure 34) and Monroe on 17 (their 18). Against stage 1 it is ahead on all 18 Biogen combinations and 14 of 27 ExpansionRx ones, behind on one, a median +0.067 R² on Biogen and +0.024 on ExpansionRx. Re-training stage 1 on the new GPU moves it by at most 0.007 R². On the 85% of Biogen test molecules PCBA does not contain, Bio still beats stage 1 on every endpoint.
